title: Absolutus_V3 (modbench): cardinality-constrained module selection benchmark on biological networks
description:
Absolutus_V3 (modbench) is an open, reproducible benchmark and toolkit for cardinality-constrained module selection (QUBO / densest-k-subgraph style) on biologically structured networks.

It compares classical solvers (random, greedy, simulated annealing, tabu, exact MILP via HiGHS) against QAOA with statevector and MPS (tensor-network) simulation at equal compute (30 s wall-clock and 10,000 QUBO evaluations, both reported). Instances include planted ground truth and a decoy-hub null model to expose degree/study-bias artefacts.

v0.1.0 contents: 300 frozen instances (3 families × 5 sizes × 20 test seeds; sha256 manifest at results/instances/manifest.json); 114 aggregated result cells with 20 seeds each and 95% bootstrap CIs; a claims register (docs/CLAIMS.md) where every claim cites a saved run; and honest documentation of every regime where classical baselines beat QAOA.
